message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality data, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  
For the most up‑to‑date information you can check one of the following:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the current AQI, pollutant levels, and health advisories. |
| **AQICN** | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles”, and see the real‑time AQI, forecast, and historical trends. |
| **Local news sites** | Many local stations (e.g., KABC, KTLA) publish live air‑quality dashboards. |
| **Mobile apps** | Apps like “AirVisual” or “Plume Labs: Air Report” provide real‑time readings and alerts. |

If you need a quick snapshot, you can also use voice assistants (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They pull from the same public APIs.

We can approximate or say we don't have real-time data. We could suggest checking an API or website. We might use a placeholder. There's no function to get air quality. So we respond with a general answer: we can't fetch real-time data. Suggest checking AirNow or local sources.
